AssayDetails: Buffer scrub samples from the scalps of healthy and dandruff individuals pre and post treatment with an antifungal containing shampoo.
objectives: Dandruff is a cosmetic condition of the scalp characterised by visible flaking, and is experienced by up to half of consumers during their lifetime. To build our knowledge and understanding of scalp condition and dandruff in general, it is important that we explore the biological scalp profiles of subjects with and without visible dandruff flakes.  Initial investigations have shown that there are key differences in the transcriptome, epigenome, microbiota and other biomarkers in the scalps of subjects with visible dandruff flakes as compared to the scalps of subjects with visually healthy scalps (very low incidence of visible flaking).    This study is designed to investigate biological markers and mechanisms in the skin following dandruff flake resolution, by determining the differences, if any, in the transcriptomic and epigenetic profiles of subjects with visible dandruff flakes as compared to the scalps of subjects with visually healthy scalps after 4 weeks regular use of an anti-dandruff (AD) shampoo.  This ELN record has been created to facilitate the analysis of scalp metataxonomic experiments from samples in study HAI-BIO-3252. This record deals with analysis of fungal communities.
